definition.simple: Choosing how big a trade is so that hitting the stop loses only the amount you planned.
definition.balanced: Size in lots = money at risk ÷ (stop distance in pips × [[pip-value]] for 1 lot). Round down to your broker's size step, so the real risk stays at or under the plan. Costs such as the [[spread]] add to the loss.

example: Example: risk 100 USD, stop 40 pips, pip value 10 USD per lot. Size = 100 ÷ (40 × 10) = 0.25 lot.
